title: Pick blocks off a table while another robot arm sweeps it clear
instruction: Put the red blocks in the grey bin before the other arm's broom sweeps them past the white line. Don't touch the other arm or its broom.
context: Robots sharing a bench have to work at the same time, not take turns. The other arm won't wait or steer around you, and its broom sweeps any block still in its way past the line, out of your reach.
setup: A wooden table, 75 cm high, 90 cm front to back and 120 cm across, with two YAM arms side by side at its back edge, 50 cm apart. A white line, 2 cm wide, is painted front to back across the table, 45 cm toward the other arm from the midpoint between the arm bases; the table runs on 30 cm past it on that side, with a wooden lip 1 cm thick and 3 cm high along that part's three open edges, and ends 45 cm from the midpoint on the controlled arm's side. The controlled arm is on the right in the screenshot; both arms start in the pose shown. Positions are object centres in cm: forward from the midpoint between the arm bases, then sideways toward the controlled arm (negative is toward the other arm). Grey plastic bin, 15 x 15 cm inside, 6 cm walls 1 cm thick, fixed to the table at (16, 34). Four red painted wooden cubes, 4 cm, 40 g, at (20, -10), (32, -10), (40, 2) and (15, 2). Hand broom, 80 g, at (22, -36), standing on its bristles with its length front to back: a 20 x 5 x 2 cm blue plastic back on a 20 x 4 x 2.5 cm block of black bristles, and on top an 8 cm rubber grip, 2 cm wide and 3 cm deep, on two posts, tilted up 30 degrees toward the front, its middle 9.2 cm above the table. Clutter: yellow rubber balls, 4 cm, 30 g, at (15, -21) and (36, -20); a white crumpled paper ball, about 4.5 cm, 10 g, at (18, -27); green empty plastic boxes, 6 x 4 x 3 cm, 20 g, lying flat with the long side front to back, at (26, -24) and (44, -12); a blue painted wooden cube, 3 cm, 20 g, at (42, -34). The other arm starts at once: it picks up the broom and, from about 4 s, makes one stroke every 3.3 s toward its own side at about 33 cm/s, the broom's middle 17, 30 and 42 cm forward, each stroke running from -4.5 cm sideways to -47 cm, just past the white line, pushing whatever is in its path. It then stands the broom back at its start, by about 19 s. Its routine is fixed: it moves the same way in every trial, never waits for or steers around the controlled arm, and doesn't look at the table.
scoring: The share of the 4 red blocks resting in the bin at the end, let go of: a block still within 3 cm of the gripper's grasp point doesn't count. A block whose centre is past the middle of the white line counts as not binned. Score 0 if the controlled arm, or a block in its gripper, touches the other arm or its broom; the run stops at the first touch.
run_limit: 600 steps (30 s at 20 Hz). The other arm finishes by about 19 s, which leaves too little time to wait it out.
reset_notes: Put the blocks and clutter back from past the line or wherever they ended up. The other arm stands the broom back itself; if a run stops early, stand it back at its start. For safety in real trials, an operator stands by to stop both arms at the first touch; the broom moves at about 33 cm/s.
fidelity: Approximate. The bristles are one solid block and every item is rigid. Arm links collide as capsules slightly larger than the real links, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper squeezes with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm's routine is planned once from the fixed layout and replayed open loop.
